problem_severity.instructions: How severe is the problem this fix addresses?
criteria: not a real problem — false positive or theoretical concern with no concrete impact
minor — cosmetic, edge case rarely hit, or negligible user/system impact
moderate — affects correctness, reliability, or developer experience in real scenarios
critical — data loss, security vulnerability, production failure, or blocks core functionality

fix_necessity.instructions: Is this fix necessary, or can the problem be safely left as-is?

criteria.must_fix: Problem will cause real harm if not fixed now — users, data, security, or core flow affected
criteria.should_fix: Problem is real and worth fixing in this PR — improves correctness or quality meaningfully
criteria.can_defer: Problem is real but low-urgency — fix in a follow-up or when the area is next touched
criteria.skip_fix: Problem is not worth fixing — cost of change exceeds benefit, or the issue is acceptable

net_value.instructions: After considering the problem severity, fix quality, and change cost — what is the net value of applying this fix?
criteria: negative — the fix causes more problems than it solves (regression risk, complexity, churn)
neutral — the fix is correct but barely worth the diff (cosmetic, no measurable impact)
positive — the fix clearly improves the codebase with reasonable effort
high — the fix prevents real harm or delivers significant user/system value
